newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans end up on El Nino, commercial buying.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans end up on El Nino, commercial buying.

text.p: Fears about the potential for drought caused by a strengthening El Nino weather pattern pushed CBOT soybeans to end higher Wednesday, traders said.
"The El Nino is bullish because it might mean fewer crops in the long term," said one floor trader.
On Tuesday, the U.S. National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration said an El Nino weather pattern was in progress and it would likely affect world crop development.
El Nino has the potential to produce drought-like conditions in southeast Asia, Australia and India, which could threaten oilseed and grain crops, Oil World newsletter said.
However, some meteorologists said the weather pattern's effect on U.S. crops was unclear.
"There is nothing conclusive, at least not in the (U.S.) grain areas," said Mike Palmerino, meteorologist with Weather Services Corp in Lexington, Mass.
Large-scale commercial buying in nearby contracts also contributed to the market's strength, traders said.
July soybeans settled up 17-1/2 cents per bushel higher at $8.30-1/2, with other months 4-1/2 to 12-3/4 cents higher.
Early in the session, trade was choppy ahead of the U.S. Department of Agriculture's Supply and Demand report to be released at 0730 CDT/1230 GMT on Thursday.
Analysts were looking for the government to possibly increase U.S. imports and and raise the crush. Few expect USDA to change the already-low old-crop ending stocks figure of 125 million bushels.
Weekly crushing data from the National Oilseed Processors Association and weekly export sales data will also be released on Thursday.
Traders expected old-crop soybean export sales of 50,000 to 100,000 tonnes. New crop sales were expected to come in between 200,000 to 400,000 tonnes, traders and analysts said.
On the day, Cargill bought four million bushels July and one million August. Tenco sold 2.5 million July and Refco bought 1.5 million November.
In options trade, FIMAT Futures, Inc. sold 1,500 August $8.00 calls and Lind-Waldock bought 500 November $6.25 puts and sold 500 August $8.50 calls, floor sources said.
Soybean futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 61,000 contracts. That figure compared with Tuesday's actual volume of 59,854, according to CBOT data.
